nodes.name: Dictionary learning (sparse coding) model
nodes.statement_short: Data $y_{(j)}=A^*x^*_{(j)}$ generated from an unknown dictionary $A^*$ and $k$-sparse coefficients.

nodes.name: Sparse generative model y = A* x*
nodes.statement_short: Each sample is $A^*$ times a $k$-sparse coefficient vector.
nodes.label: eq:model

nodes.name: Regularized least squares dictionary learning objective (P1)
nodes.statement: \tag{P1} \textstyle \min\limits_{\b{A}, \cbr{\b{x}_{(j)}}_{j=1}^p } \sum\limits_{j = 1}^{p}\|\b{y}_{(j)} - \b{A}\b{x}_{(j)}\|^2_2 + \sum\limits_{j=1}^{p}S(\b{x}_{(j)}).\vspace*{-2pt}
nodes.statement_short: Minimize squared reconstruction error plus a sparsity-promoting penalty $S(\cdot)$ over $A$ and the $x_{(j)}$.
nodes.label: eq:objective

nodes.name: Local minimum of the l1 dictionary learning program (Gribonval-Schnass)
assumptions: with high probability over the randomness of the coefficients
conclusions: the solution pair \[\rbr{\b{A}^*, \b{X}^*}\] lies at a local minima of the following non-convex optimization program
nodes.statement_short: For square dictionaries the true pair is w.h.p. a local minimum of the l1-minimization DL program.

nodes.name: l1-minimization dictionary learning program
nodes.statement: \underset{\b{A}, \b{X}}{\rm min}~\|\b{X}\|_1 ~~~\text{s.t.}~ \b{Y} = \b{AX}, ~~~\|\b{A}_i\| = 1, \forall ~i \in [m].
nodes.statement_short: Minimize $\|X\|_1$ subject to $Y=AX$ with unit-norm dictionary columns.
nodes.label: eq:alt_min_obj

nodes.name: [n] notation
nodes.statement: Given an integer $n$, we denote $[n] = \cbr{1, 2,\ldots,n}$.

nodes.name: O* notation
nodes.statement: Further, we use \[g(n) = \mathcal{O}^*(f(n))\] to indicate that \[g(n) \leq L f(n)\] for a small enough constant \[L\], which is independent of \[n\].

nodes.name: Hard-thresholding operator
nodes.statement: \[{\c{T}}_{\tau}(z) := z\cdot\mathbbm{1}_{|z|\geq \tau}\] denotes the hard-thresholding operator, where ``\[\mathbbm{1}\]'' is the indicator function.

nodes.name: Support and sign notation
nodes.statement: We use \[{\rm supp}(\cdot)\] for the support (the set of non-zero elements) and \[{\rm sign}(\cdot)\] for the element-wise sign.

nodes.name: (epsilon, kappa)-closeness
nodes.statement: \textit{A dictionary \[\b{A}\] is \[(\epsilon, \kappa)\]-close to \[\b{A}^*\] if \[\|\b{A} - \b{A}^*\| \leq \kappa\|\b{A}^*\|\], and if there is a permutation \[\pi: [m] \rightarrow [m]\] and a collection of signs \[\sigma: [m] \rightarrow \{\pm 1\}\] such that \[\|\sigma(i)\b{A}_{\pi(i)} - \b{A}^*_i\|\leq \epsilon, ~\forall~ i\in [m]\].}\vspace{-3pt}
nodes.statement_short: A is close to A* in spectral norm (within kappa||A*||) and column-wise (within epsilon) up to permutation and sign.
nodes.label: def:del_kappa

nodes.name: NOODL (Neurally plausible alternating Optimization-based Online Dictionary Learning)
nodes.statement_short: Online alternating method: IHT-based coefficient estimation (Predict) then an approximate gradient step on the dictionary with column normalization (Learn).
input: Fresh data samples \[\b{y}_{(j)} \in \mathbb{R}^{n} \] for \[j \in [p]\] at each iteration \[t\]
output: The dictionary \[\b{A}^{(t)}\] and coefficient estimates \[\hat{\b{x}}_{(j)}^{(t)} \] for \[j \in [p]\] at each iterate \[t\]
nodes.label: alg:main_alg

nodes.name: Hard-thresholding coefficient initialization
nodes.statement_short: Initial coefficients: hard-threshold $A^{(t)\top}y$ at $C/2$.
nodes.label: alg:coeff_init

nodes.name: IHT coefficient update
nodes.statement_short: Gradient step on coefficients followed by hard thresholding at $\tau^{(r)}$.
nodes.label: alg:coeff_iht

nodes.name: Empirical gradient estimate
nodes.statement: &\hspace{0.14in}\text{Form empirical gradient estimate:}~~\hat{\b{g}}^{(t)} = \tfrac{1}{p}\textstyle\sum_{j = 1}^{p}(\b{A}^{(t)}\hat{\b{x}}_{(j)}^{(t)}   - \b{y}_{(j)}){\rm sign}(\hat{\b{x}}_{(j)}^{(t)}  )^\top&
nodes.statement_short: Average of residual times sign of coefficient estimates over the mini-batch.
nodes.label: eq:emp_grad_est

nodes.name: Dictionary gradient descent step
nodes.statement: &\hspace{0.14in}\text{Take a gradient descent step:}~~\b{A}^{(t+1)} = \b{A}^{(t)} - \eta_A~\hat{\b{g}}^{(t)}&
nodes.label: eq:apx_grad

nodes.name: Outer loop over online iterations t
nodes.statement_short: Outer online iteration over mini-batches.

nodes.name: Loop over samples j
nodes.statement_short: For each sample in the mini-batch, estimate its coefficients.

nodes.name: Coefficient initialization by hard thresholding
nodes.statement_short: Initialize coefficients by hard-thresholding $A^{(t)\top}y_{(j)}$ at $C/2$.

nodes.name: IHT loop over r
nodes.statement_short: Run R iterative hard thresholding steps.

nodes.name: IHT update
nodes.statement_short: Gradient step on the coefficients followed by hard thresholding.

nodes.name: Set coefficient estimate and learn dictionary
nodes.statement_short: Take the R-th IHT iterate as estimate, form the empirical gradient, take a gradient step on the dictionary and normalize columns.

nodes.name: Target tolerance delta_R for IHT
nodes.statement: Given this initial estimate $\b{x}^{(0)}$, the algorithm iterates over  \[R= \Omega(\log(1/\delta_{R}))\] IHT-based steps \eqref{alg:coeff_iht} to achieve a target tolerance of \[\delta_{R}\], such that \[(1 - \eta_{x})^{R} \leq \delta_{R}\].
nodes.statement_short: R IHT steps achieve target tolerance $\delta_R$ with $(1-\eta_x)^R\le\delta_R$.

nodes.name: IHT step size and threshold
nodes.statement: Here, \[\eta_{x}^{(r)}\] is the learning rate, and \[\tau^{(r)}\] is the threshold at the \[r\]-th iterate of the IHT.

nodes.name: Coefficient estimate x-hat
nodes.statement: Finally at the end of this stage, we have estimate \[\hat{\b{x}}^{(t)} :=\b{x}^{(R)}\] of \[\b{x}^*\].

nodes.name: Per-iteration running time of NOODL
nodes.statement: The running time of each step \[t\] of NOODL is therefore \[\mathcal{O}(mnp \log(1/\delta_{R}))\].

nodes.name: Signed-support
nodes.statement: \textit{The signed-support of a vector \[\b{x}\] is defined as \[{\rm sign}(\b{x})\cdot {\rm supp}(\b{x})\].}
nodes.statement_short: Signed-support of x: sign(x) times supp(x).
nodes.label: def:signed-support

nodes.name: Column-wise dictionary error epsilon_t
nodes.statement: Further, in our analysis, we ensure \[\epsilon_t\] (defined as \[\|\b{A}_i^{(t)} - \b{A}^*_i\| \leq \epsilon_t\]) contracts at every iteration, and assume \[\epsilon_0, \epsilon_t = \mathcal{O}^*(1/\log(n))\].

nodes.name: mu-incoherence
nodes.statement: \textit{ A matrix \[\b{A} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times m}\] with unit-norm columns is \[\mu\]-incoherent if for all \[{i \neq j}\] the inner-product between the columns of the matrix follow \[ |\langle \b{A}_i, \b{A}_j\rangle| \leq \mu/\sqrt{n}\].}
nodes.label: def:mu

nodes.name: Distribution class D of the coefficients
nodes.statement: \textit{The coefficient vector \[\b{x}^*\] belongs to an unknown distribution \[\c{D}\], where the support \[S = {\rm supp}(\b{x}^*)\] is at most of size \[k\], \[\b{Pr}[i \in S] = \Theta(k/m)\] and \[\b{Pr}[i, j \in S] = \Theta(k^2/m^2)\]. Moreover, the distribution is normalized such that \[\b{E}[\b{x}_i^*|i \in S] = 0\] and \[\b{E}[\b{x}_i^{*^2}|i \in S] = 1\], and when \[i \in S\],  \[|\b{x}^*_i| \geq C\] for some constant \[C \leq 1\]. In addition, the non-zero entries are sub-Gaussian and pairwise independent conditioned on the support.}
nodes.statement_short: Support of size at most k with Theta(k/m) marginals and Theta(k^2/m^2) pairwise; zero-mean unit-variance sub-Gaussian non-zeros bounded below by C.
nodes.label: dist_x

nodes.name: Relaxing the lower bound on coefficient magnitudes
nodes.statement: Note that, although we only consider the case \[|\b{x}^*_i | \geq C\] for ease of discussion, analogous results may hold more generally for \[\b{x}_i^*\]’s drawn from a distribution with sufficiently (exponentially) small probability of taking values in \[[-C, C]\].

nodes.name: (rho-, rho+, zeta)-correlation with a descent direction
nodes.statement_short: Local descent condition: inner product of g with z - z* dominates rho- ||z-z*||^2 + rho+ ||g||^2 - zeta.
nodes.label: def:grad_alpha_beta

nodes.name: Correlation condition implied by strong convexity and smoothness
nodes.statement: In convex optimization literature, this condition is implied by the \[2\rho_{-}\]-strong convexity, and \[1/2\rho_{_+}\]-smoothness of the objective.

nodes.name: A.1 Incoherent dictionary
nodes.statement: \[\b{A}^*\] is \[\mu\]-incoherent (Def.~\ref{def:mu}), where \[\mu = \mathcal{O}(\log(n))\], \[\|\b{A}^*\| = \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{m/n})\] and \[m = \mathcal{O}(n)\];

nodes.name: A.2 Coefficient distribution
nodes.statement: The coefficients are drawn from the distribution class \[\c{D}\], as per Def.~\ref{dist_x};

nodes.name: A.3 Sparsity level
nodes.statement:
The sparsity \[k\] satisfies \[k = \mathcal{O}({\sqrt{n}}/{\mu~\log(n)})\];
\item \[\b{A}^{(0)}\] is \[(\epsilon_0, 2)\]-close to \[\b{A}^*\]  as per Def.~\ref{def:del_kappa}, and \[\epsilon_0 = \mathcal{O}^*(1/\log(n))\];

nodes.name: A.4 Initialization closeness
nodes.statement: \[\b{A}^{(0)}\] is \[(\epsilon_0, 2)\]-close to \[\b{A}^*\]  as per Def.~\ref{def:del_kappa}, and \[\epsilon_0 = \mathcal{O}^*(1/\log(n))\];

nodes.name: A.5 Dictionary step size
nodes.statement: The step-size for dictionary update satisfies \[\eta_A = \Theta(m/k)\];

nodes.name: A.6 Coefficient step size and threshold
nodes.statement: The step-size and threshold for coefficient estimation satisfies \[\eta_x^{(r)}< c_1(\epsilon_t, \mu, n, k) = \tilde{\Omega}({k}/{\sqrt{n}})<1\] and \[\tau^{(r)} = c_2(\epsilon_t, \mu, k, n) = \tilde{\Omega}({k^2}/{n})\] for small constants \[c_1\] and \[c_2\].

nodes.name: Main Result: exact geometric recovery of dictionary and coefficients by NOODL
assumptions: Algorithm~\ref{alg:main_alg} is provided with  \[ p = \tilde{\Omega}(mk^2)\] new samples generated according to model \eqref{eq:model} at each iteration \[t\]
conclusions: the coefficient estimate \[\hat{\b{x}}_{i}^{(t)}\] at \[t\]-th iteration has the correct signed-support
nodes.statement_short: Under A.1-A.6 with p = Omega~(mk^2) samples per iteration, NOODL recovers signed supports and both factors converge geometrically, without bias.
nodes.label: main_result

nodes.name: Noise tolerance of NOODL
nodes.statement: Also, note that, NOODL can tolerate i.i.d. noise, as long as the noise variance is controlled to enable the concentration results to hold; we consider the noiseless case here for ease of discussion, which is already highly involved.

nodes.name: Overall running time and sample complexity of NOODL
nodes.statement: NOODL has an overall running time of \[\mathcal{O}(mnp \log(1/\delta_{R})\max(\log(1/\epsilon_{T}), \log(\sqrt{k}/\delta_T))\] to achieve target tolerances \[\epsilon_{T} \]  and \[\delta_T\], with a total sample complexity of \[ p \cdot T  = \tilde{\Omega}(mk^2)\].
conclusions: NOODL has an overall running time of \[\mathcal{O}(mnp \log(1/\delta_{R})\max(\log(1/\epsilon_{T}), \log(\sqrt{k}/\delta_T))\]
with a total sample complexity of \[ p \cdot T  = \tilde{\Omega}(mk^2)\]

nodes.name: Neural implementation of NOODL
nodes.statement:
\noindent\textbf{Initial Hard Thresholding Phase}: The coefficients initialized to zero, and an input \[(\b{y}_{(j)}, 1)\] is provided to the input layer at a time instant \[\ell=0\], which communicates these to the second layer. Therefore, the residual at the output of the weighted residual evaluation layer evaluates to \[\b{y}_{(j)}\] at \[\ell=1\]. Next, at \[\ell=2\], this residual is communicated to the output layer, which results in evaluation of the initialization \[ \b{x}_{(j)}^{(0)}\] as per \eqref{alg:coeff_init}. This iterate is communicated to the second layer for the next residual evaluation. Also, at this time, the input layer is injected with  \[(\b{y}_{(j)}, \eta_x)\] to set the step size parameter \[\eta_x\] for the IHT phase, as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:neural_imple}(b). 

\noindent\textbf{Iterative Hard Thresholding (IHT) Phase}: Beginning \[\ell =3\], the timing sequence enters the IHT phase. Here, the output layer neurons communicate the iterates \[\b{x}^{(r+1)}_{(j)}\] to the second layer for evaluation of subsequent iterates as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:neural_imple}(b). The process then continues till the time instance \[\ell = 2R+1\], for \[{R} = \Omega(\log(1/\delta_{R}))\] to generate the final coefficient estimate \[ \widehat{\b{x}}_{(j)}^{(t)} := \b{x}_{(j)}^{(R)} \] for the current batch of data. At this time, the input layer is again injected with \[(\b{y}_{(j)}, 1)\] to prepare the network for residual sharing and gradient evaluation for dictionary update.

\noindent\textbf{Dictionary Update Phase:} The procedure now enters the dictionary update phase, denoted as ``Hebbian Learning'' in the timing sequence. In this phase, each output layer neuron communicates the final coefficient estimate \[ \widehat{\b{x}}_{(j)}^{(t)} = \b{x}_{(j)}^{(R)} \] to the second layer, which evaluates the residual for one last time (with \[\eta_x =1\]), and shares it across all second layer neurons (``Hebbian learning''). This allows each second layer neuron to evaluate the empirical gradient estimate \eqref{eq:emp_grad_est},



which is used to update the current dictionary estimate (stored as weights) via an approximate gradient descent step. This completes one outer iteration of Algorithm~\ref{alg:main_alg}, and the process continues for \[T\] iterations to achieve target tolerances \[\epsilon_T\] and \[\delta_T\], with each step receiving a new mini-batch of data.
nodes.statement_short: Three-layer neural timing scheme: initial hard-thresholding phase, IHT phase over 2R+1 time steps, then Hebbian dictionary update.

nodes.name: Initial hard thresholding phase
nodes.statement: \noindent\textbf{Initial Hard Thresholding Phase}: The coefficients initialized to zero, and an input \[(\b{y}_{(j)}, 1)\] is provided to the input layer at a time instant \[\ell=0\], which communicates these to the second layer. Therefore, the residual at the output of the weighted residual evaluation layer evaluates to \[\b{y}_{(j)}\] at \[\ell=1\]. Next, at \[\ell=2\], this residual is communicated to the output layer, which results in evaluation of the initialization \[ \b{x}_{(j)}^{(0)}\] as per \eqref{alg:coeff_init}. This iterate is communicated to the second layer for the next residual evaluation. Also, at this time, the input layer is injected with  \[(\b{y}_{(j)}, \eta_x)\] to set the step size parameter \[\eta_x\] for the IHT phase, as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:neural_imple}(b).
nodes.statement_short: Feed (y,1), compute residual y, and output the hard-thresholded initialization.

nodes.name: IHT phase
nodes.statement: \noindent\textbf{Iterative Hard Thresholding (IHT) Phase}: Beginning \[\ell =3\], the timing sequence enters the IHT phase. Here, the output layer neurons communicate the iterates \[\b{x}^{(r+1)}_{(j)}\] to the second layer for evaluation of subsequent iterates as shown in Fig.~\ref{fig:neural_imple}(b). The process then continues till the time instance \[\ell = 2R+1\], for \[{R} = \Omega(\log(1/\delta_{R}))\] to generate the final coefficient estimate \[ \widehat{\b{x}}_{(j)}^{(t)} := \b{x}_{(j)}^{(R)} \] for the current batch of data. At this time, the input layer is again injected with \[(\b{y}_{(j)}, 1)\] to prepare the network for residual sharing and gradient evaluation for dictionary update.
nodes.statement_short: Output neurons iterate the IHT update until time 2R+1.

nodes.name: Dictionary update phase (Hebbian learning)
nodes.statement:
\noindent\textbf{Dictionary Update Phase:} The procedure now enters the dictionary update phase, denoted as ``Hebbian Learning'' in the timing sequence. In this phase, each output layer neuron communicates the final coefficient estimate \[ \widehat{\b{x}}_{(j)}^{(t)} = \b{x}_{(j)}^{(R)} \] to the second layer, which evaluates the residual for one last time (with \[\eta_x =1\]), and shares it across all second layer neurons (``Hebbian learning''). This allows each second layer neuron to evaluate the empirical gradient estimate \eqref{eq:emp_grad_est},



which is used to update the current dictionary estimate (stored as weights) via an approximate gradient descent step. This completes one outer iteration of Algorithm~\ref{alg:main_alg}, and the process continues for \[T\] iterations to achieve target tolerances \[\epsilon_T\] and \[\delta_T\], with each step receiving a new mini-batch of data.
nodes.statement_short: Share the final residual and update the dictionary weights via the empirical gradient.

nodes.name: Upper-bound on the error in coefficient estimation
nodes.statement:
With probability at least \[(1 - \delta_{\beta}^{(t)} - \delta_{{\c{T}}}^{(t)})\] the error incurred by each element \[i_1 \in {\rm supp}(\b{x}^*)\] of the coefficient estimate is upper-bounded as
 	\begin{align*}
 	
 	
 	|\hat{\b{x}}_{i_1} - \b{x}_{i_1}^*|
 
 	&\leq    \mathcal{O}(t_\beta) + \left({(R + 1)}k \eta_x\tfrac{\mu_t}{\sqrt{n}}~\underset{i}{\max}|\b{x}_{i}^{(0)} - \b{x}_{i}^*| + |\b{x}_{i_1}^{(0)} - \b{x}_{i_1}^*| \right)\delta_{R},
 	
 	=  \mathcal{O}(t_\beta)
 	\end{align*}
 	
 	where \[t_\beta = \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{k\epsilon_t})\], \[\delta_{R} := (1 - \eta_{x} + \eta_x\tfrac{\mu_t}{\sqrt{n}})^{R}\], \[\delta_{{\c{T}}}^{(t)} = 2m~{\exp}({-\tfrac{C^2}{\mathcal{O}^*(\epsilon_t^2)}})\], \[\delta_{\beta}^{(t)} = 2k~{\exp}(-\tfrac{1}{\mathcal{O}(\epsilon_t)})\], and \[\mu_t\] is the incoherence between the columns of \[\b{A}^{(t)}\]; see Claim~\ref{claim:incoherence of B}.

nodes.name: A^(t+1) maintains closeness
nodes.statement:
Suppose \[\b{A}^{(t)}\] is \[(\epsilon_t, 2)\] near to \[\b{A}^*\] with \[\epsilon_t = \mathcal{O}^*(1/\log(n))\], and number of samples used in step \[t\] is \[p = \tilde{\Omega}(mk^2)\], then with probability at least \[(1 - \delta_{{\c{T}}}^{(t)} - \delta_{\beta}^{(t)}

nodes.statement_short: Combine the correlation lemma and closeness lemma with Arora et al.'s Theorem 40 for geometric dictionary convergence; coefficient error follows from the coefficient error lemma.

nodes.name: Correlation and closeness
nodes.statement: From Lemma~\ref{grad_corr} we have that with probability at least \[(1 - \delta_{{\c{T}}}^{(t)} - \delta_{\beta}^{(t)} - \delta_{\rm HW}^{(t)} -\delta_{\b{g}_i}^{(t)})\], \[\b{g}^{(t)}_j\] is \[(\Omega(k/m), \Omega(m/k),0 )\]-correlated with \[\b{A}^*_j\]. Further, Lemma~\ref{lem:closeness} ensures that each iterate maintains the closeness property.
nodes.statement_short: Gradient is correlated with the descent direction and closeness is maintained.

Here, \[\delta_{\text{alg}}^{(t)}  = \delta_{{\c{T}}}^{(t)} + \delta_{\beta}^{(t)} + \delta_{\rm HW}^{(t)} +\delta_{\b{g}_i}^{(t)} + \delta_{\b{g}}^{(t)})\]. nodes.name: Proof of Lemma (signed-support recovery by initialization)

nodes.name: Decompose inner product
nodes.statement:
Let \[\b{y} \in \mathbb{R}^{n}\] be general sample generated as \[\b{y} = \b{A}^*\b{x}^*\], where \[\b{x}^* \in \mathbb{R}^{m}\] is a sparse random vector with support \[S = {\rm supp}(\b{x}^*)\] distributed according to \textbf{D.\ref{dist_x}}.
	
	The initial decoding step at the \[t\]-th iteration (shown in Algorithm~\ref{alg:main_alg}) involves evaluating the inner-product between the estimate of the dictionary \[\b{A}^{(t)}\], and \[\b{y}\]. The \[i\]-th element of the resulting vector can be written as
	\begin{align*}
	\langle \b{A}_i^{(t)}, \b{y}\rangle &= 	
	\langle \b{A}_i^{(t)}, \b{A}^*_i \rangle \b{x}^*_i + \b{w}_i,
	\end{align*}
	
	where \[\b{w}_i =  \langle \b{A}_i^{(t)}, \b{A}^*_{-i}\b{x}^*_{-i}\rangle \].
nodes.statement_short: Introduce a sample and decompose the i-th inner product into signal plus interference w_i.

nodes.statement:
Consider the \[(r+1)\]-th iterate \[\b{x}^{(r+1)}\] for the \[t\]-th dictionary iterate, where \[\|\b{A}^{(t)}_i - \b{A}^*_i\|\leq \epsilon_t\] for all \[i \in [1, m]\] evaluated as the following by the update step described in Algorithm~\ref{alg:main_alg},
	\begin{align} \b{x}^{(r+1)} &= \b{x}^{(r)} - \eta_{x}^{(r+1)}\b{A}^{(t)^\top}(\b{A}^{(t)}\b{x}^{(r)} - \b{y}) \notag\\
	&= (\b{I} - \eta_{x}^{(r+1)}\b{A}^{(t)^\top}\b{A}^{(t)})\b{x}^{(r)} - \eta_{x}^{(r+1)}\b{A}^{(t)^\top}\b{A}^*\b{x}^*,
	\end{align}
	
	where \[\eta_{x}^{(1)} < 1\] is the learning rate or the step-size parameter.

nodes.statement: Let \[\b{w}_j = \b{z}_j  - \b{E}[\b{z}]\], we will now apply the vector Bernstein result shown in Lemma~\ref{vector_bernstein}. nodes.name: Verify correlation
nodes.statement:
Now, we show that this gradient is \[(\rho_{\_}, 1/100\rho_{\_}, 0)\] correlated,
				\begin{align*}
				\langle\hat{\b{g}}^{(t)}_i, \b{A}^{(t)}_i - &\b{A}^*_i\rangle - \rho_{\_} \|\b{A}^{(t)}_i - \b{A}^*_i\|^2 - \tfrac{1}{100\rho_{\_}}\|\hat{\b{g}}^{(t)}_i\|^2, \\
				&\geq 4\rho_{\_} \|\b{A}^{(t)}_i - \b{A}^*_i\|^2 - \|\tilde{v}\| \|\b{A}^{(t)}_i - \b{A}^*_i\|  - \rho_{\_} \|\b{A}^{(t)}_i - \b{A}^*_i\|^2 - \tfrac{1}{100\rho_{\_}}\|\hat{\b{g}}^{(t)}_i\|^2, \\
				&\geq 4\rho_{\_} \|\b{A}^{(t)}_i - \b{A}^*_i\|^2 - 2\rho_{\_} \|\b{A}^{(t)}_i - \b{A}^*_i\|^2 -\tfrac{25\rho_{\_}^2 \|\b{A}^{(t)}_i - \b{A}^*_i\|^2}{100\rho_{\_}},\\
				&\geq \rho_{\_} \|\b{A}^{(t)}_i - \b{A}^*_i\|^2  \geq 0.
				\end{align*}
				
			Therefore, for this choice of \[k\], i.e.  \[k = \c{O} (\sqrt{n})\], there is no bias in dictionary estimation in comparison to \cite{Arora15}. This gain can be attributed to estimating the coefficients simultaneously with the dictionary.

Now, we are ready to apply the matrix Bernstein result. Since, \[m = O(n)\] the variance statistic comes out to be \[\mathcal{O}(\tfrac{k^3t_{\beta}^2}{pm})\|\b{A}^*\|^2\], then as long as we choose \[p = \tilde{\Omega}(mk^2)\] (using the bound on \[t_\beta\]), with probability at least \[(1 - \delta_{\beta}^{(t)} - \delta_{{\c{T}}}^{(t)} - \delta_{\rm HW}^{(t)} - \delta_{\b{g}}^{(t)})\]
	\begin{align*}
	\|\hat{\b{g}}^{(t)} -  \b{g}^{(t)}\| &\leq 	\mathcal{O}(\tfrac{k\sqrt{k}}{p}t_{\beta}) + 
\|\b{A}^*\|\sqrt{\mathcal{O}(\tfrac{k^3t_{\beta}^2}{pm})},\\ 
	&= \mathcal{O}^*(\tfrac{k}{m}  \|\b{A}^*\| ).
	\end{align*}
	
	where \[\delta_{\b{g}}^{(t)} = (n+m)\exp(-\Omega(m\sqrt{\log(n)})\].
